extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), corporate counsel, compliance officers, and investors preparing or evaluating SEC climate-related disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule requirements for U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) climate-related disclosures by registrants, covering management oversight, risk management (Item 1503), and targets/goals (Item 1504).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe relevant expertise of position holders
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a description of the relevant expertise of position holders or members responsible for assessing and managing climate-related risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of expertise is required only where the risk is material; this helps investors understand a registrant's ability to manage material climate-related risks. The rule was adopted while recognizing concerns that such disclosure could pressure hiring practices, but the materiality qualifier mitigates that concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process-based description of management's governance of material climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a non-exclusive, process-focused description of management's role in assessing and managing the registrant's material climate-related risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include describing the processes by which certain positions or committees are informed about and monitor climate-related risks. A process-based description offers investors a meaningful look at how management oversees material climate risks. Registrants may tailor which details to include based on facts and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose whether management reports to the board or a subcommittee
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose, if applicable, whether management reports to the board or a subcommittee of the board on climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminated the proposed requirement to disclose how frequently the board meets on climate matters, but retained whether reporting to board/subcommittee occurs because it clarifies the connection between board and management governance for climate risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require disclosure of management's role in climate-related opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is not adopting the proposed rule that would have allowed, but not required, registrants to describe management's role in assessing and managing climate-related opportunities; such disclosure remains voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants may elect to include disclosures about climate-related opportunities, but the Commission determined to treat such disclosure as optional to avoid anti-competitive concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management processes for material climate-related risks (Item 1503)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a registrant to describe any processes the registrant has for identifying, assessing, and managing material climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule focuses on material risks and adopts a less prescriptive, principles-based approach so registrants can tailor disclosures to their facts and circumstances while providing investors decision-useful information about how material climate risks are identified, assessed, and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify physical vs. transition risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Address, as applicable, how the registrant identifies whether it has incurred or is reasonably likely to incur a material physical or transition risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule substitutes the more specific terms “physical risk or transition risk” to clarify that different processes/factors may apply to identifying each type and to elicit more relevant information for investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision framework for individual risks (mitigate/accept/adapt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe, as applicable, how the registrant decides whether to mitigate, accept, or adapt to a particular material climate-related risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule retains requirement to explain decision process for handling specific risks, but removed overly prescriptive requirements about how to determine mitigation steps for high-priority risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization of climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Address, as applicable, how the registrant prioritizes whether to address particular material climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investors find disclosure of how registrants prioritize climate risks vis-à-vis other risks particularly useful; registrants should explain prioritization processes relevant to material risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration into overall risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether and how the processes for identifying, assessing, and managing material climate-related risks have been integrated into the registrant's overall risk management system or processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about integration is important for investors to assess effectiveness; mandating this disclosure allows comparability of climate risks with other financial and non-financial risks and signals whether climate risk management is centralized or disintegrated from enterprise risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality qualifier for all risk management disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a materiality qualifier: the final rule requires disclosure only for processes relating to material climate-related risks (no disclosure is required if the registrant has not identified a material climate risk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The materiality qualifier addresses concerns about undue cost and prescriptiveness; it aims to elicit decision-useful information without imposing burdens related to immaterial matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removed/Not-required prescriptive items
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule removed several proposed prescriptive disclosure items, including: (a) how the registrant determines the relative significance of climate-related risks compared to other risks; (b) how it considers existing or likely regulatory requirements/policies such as GHG limits; (c) how it considers shifts in customer/counterparty preferences, technological changes, or market price changes in assessing transition risks; and (d) how it determines the materiality of climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of mandating these specific items, the final rule allows registrants to determine which factors are most significant for their facts and circumstances. Also not adopted: a requirement to disclose how a separate committee interacts with the board, and not retained: the requirement to disclose how a registrant determines how to mitigate any high-priority risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculation and protection of confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are not required to speculate about future restructurings, write-downs, or impairments related to climate risks, nor to disclose trade secrets or confidential business information in their climate-related risk management disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The flexibility of the final rules helps prevent compelled disclosure of proprietary information while still eliciting decision-useful information for investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with TCFD where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule disclosures more closely align with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) risk management recommendations to promote comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment may limit costs for registrants already familiar with TCFD reporting; however, the SEC maintains a principles-based approach permitting tailoring to registrant circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets and goals disclosure when a registrant has set them (Item 1504)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a registrant that has set any climate-related targets or goals to disclose those targets or goals and, as applicable, describe specified elements of each target or goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule's examples of targets/goals include GHG reductions, energy/water usage, conservation, ecosystem restoration, or revenues from low-carbon products. The requirement is triggered only if the registrant has set targets/goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements for targets/goals description
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosing targets/goals, include, as applicable: the scope of activities and emissions included; the unit of measurement (absolute or intensity); the defined time horizon and whether it is consistent with external goals; the defined baseline time period and baseline emissions with a consistent base year across multiple targets; any interim targets; and how the registrant intends to meet its targets or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These detailed elements help investors assess the registrant's commitment level and the credibility of targets; registrants should provide sufficient specificity to permit evaluation of the target's substance and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress data and annual updates for targets/goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose relevant data indicating whether the registrant is making progress toward achieving a target or goal and how such progress has been achieved; update this disclosure each fiscal year by describing actions taken during the year to achieve targets or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic updates improve accountability and enable investors to monitor progress; some commenters supported including related capital expenditures or discrete expenditures tied to achieving targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of use of carbon offsets or RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant uses carbon offsets or renewable energy certificates (RECs) as part of any net emissions reduction strategy, disclose the role they play and, if used, the amount of carbon reduction or renewable energy represented, the source of the offsets/RECs, a description and location of the underlying projects, any registries/authentication, and the cost of the offsets/RECs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This level of detail helps prevent greenwashing and enables investors to evaluate the credibility and financial implications of offset/REC usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional/conditional practices raised by commenters
rubrics_metrics.description: Various commenter-suggested constraints and clarifications (not all adopted) include: requiring disclosure only for publicly announced targets/goals; triggering disclosure only upon formal adoption by the board or CEO; permitting registrants that have not set targets to explain why; and disclosing whether targets are science-based (e.g., SBTi) or achievable with existing technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters urged limits (e.g., only public targets) to avoid chilling internal deliberations and protect proprietary targets; the final rule balances such concerns by focusing on material, publicly relevant disclosures while allowing registrants to tailor content.
